context:
Goal: undoing a row never counts a copy twice.
Problem (rule): the rule "any row can be undone in any order" double-counts. Probe: check copy X, uncheck X, check X again. Undoing the uncheck sets X to 2 when one copy was checked, and undoing the first check erases the third.
Based on (record): mailaudit decision undo-removes-only-its-delta: a hand edit made after the row survives.
Departs from: recent-checks-can-be-undone, "any order" — a row that a later opposite write reversed can no longer be undone (a).
Meanwhile: the lane builds a; it fails toward the safe side.
holds: Which Recent rows mailaudit lets you undo.

options.how: A count row reads NOTHING TO UNDO once a later write on that card moved the count the other way, and an undo never goes above the row's own highest count.
options.label: Lock rows a later write reversed
options.lose: An old row behind a reversal cannot be undone.

options.how: Every row stays undoable in any order, as the record says today.
options.label: Keep any order
options.lose: Double counts, as the probe shows.

reply: Sent 15:30 CST to lane mailaudit-recent-log: prove the double count on today's code (a red test or a recorded run) before you pick. This comes back with the measured counts.
title: mailaudit: undoing Recent rows in any order can count a copy twice. Limit which rows can be undone?
why: A double count shows a copy as checked in when it is not.
